transcript.text:
“Not working” can mean anything from a socket or control-lock issue to a door-switch or internal fault, so the first split is whether it has any power. 1. With the microwave unplugged, check the plug is firmly connected and the wall socket is switched on. Try a known-working appliance in that socket. If that does not work either, the socket/circuit needs attention rather than the microwave.
2. If the socket is fine, plug the microwave back in and see whether its display or interior light comes on. Some models also lock the controls; look for a lock/key symbol and try holding Stop/Cancel for a few seconds.
3. If the display works, put a cup of water inside and try one minute at full power. Do not run it empty. Tell me whether it starts, makes its usual sound, and whether the water gets warm. Do not remove the microwave casing or try to inspect internal fuses: microwave high-voltage parts can retain a dangerous charge even when unplugged. Is it completely dead with no display/lights, or does the display come on but it will not start or heat?
Display is on and shows the time, door light comes on too. It beeps when I press buttons but won't start. There's a little L symbol on the display.

The little “L” is very likely the control/child-lock symbol. That would explain why the display and buttons work and beep, but the microwave will not start. 1. With the door closed, press and hold Stop/Cancel for about 3–5 seconds. On some models it is labelled Clear, Cancel or has a lock/key symbol.
2. If the L disappears, put a cup of water inside and try one minute on full power — never run it empty. If the L will not clear, or it clears but it still refuses to start, the next likely cause is the door interlock not detecting the door as shut. Do not remove the casing or attempt to bypass any door switch; that needs an appliance engineer.
ok held the stop button for 3 secs, the L has gone and it works now. thanks
That was the control/child lock, rather than a fault. If it happens again, hold Stop/Cancel for a few seconds until the L/lock symbol disappears. Is there anything else you need help with?

candidates: Power supply, plug fuse or socket issue (medium)
Control lock, clock/programme setting or control-panel problem (medium)

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
